title: Semantic-ETL-Pipeline
subtitle: Multi-Modal Ingestion & Grounded RAG Microservice
note: Layout-aware multi-modal document extraction, dual-store hybrid search (Pinecone + SQLite FTS5), and sub-30ms FlashRank reranking.
deck: An enterprise-grade, containerized multi-modal ETL and grounded RAG microservice: layout-aware Docling v2 extraction, parallel VLM diagram transcription, semchunk semantic windowing, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Pinecone 1024-d + SQLite FTS5 BM25), and local ONNX FlashRank cross-encoder reranking.

projectDetails.name: Semantic-ETL-Pipeline: Multi-Modal Ingestion & Grounded RAG
projectDetails.institution: FH Campus Wien · Enterprise AI Systems
projectDetails.summary: Increased downstream retrieval MRR by +171.0% (0.1476 → 0.4000) and reduced reranking latency by 47.5x (46,223ms → 972.68ms E2E) by replacing naive fixed-size chunking and generative LLM reranking with Docling v2 layout parsing, semchunk semantic windowing, Dual-Path Hybrid Search (Pinecone 1024-d + SQLite FTS5 BM25 via RRF), and local ONNX FlashRank cross-encoder scoring.
projectDetails.problem: Traditional PDF extraction flattens relational tables into unparseable noise, discards embedded diagrams, fractures sentences with fixed-character chunking (12 broken tables in baseline tests), and suffers 46+ second bottlenecks and 429 quota failures under generative LLM reranking.
projectDetails.solution: Achieved 100.0% structural boundary preservation (0 table fractures) and +50.0% Recall@5 lift over dense-only search (0.24 → 0.36 across 25 queries) by building an async ETL microservice with Docling v2, Azure gpt-4.1-nano VLM & metadata enrichment, SQLite WAL job persistence, asymmetric Pinecone + FTS5 RRF retrieval, and local ONNX FlashRank reranking.
projectDetails.architectureDescription: End-to-end containerized ETL and grounded RAG microservice: Docling v2 layout/table/image extraction, semaphore-bounded Azure/Groq VLM captioning, layout-preserving semchunk windowing, concurrent Pydantic metadata enrichment, dual-write indexing (Pinecone 1024-d + SQLite FTS5 BM25), RRF (k=60) + FlashRank cross-encoder retrieval, and SSE-streamed citation generation.

chapters.title: Multi-Modal Ingestion Architecture
chapters.subtitle: Layout-Aware Parsing, Image Filtering & Dual-Store Indexing
chapters.content: Eliminated visual data loss and duplicate vector writes (idempotent MD5 chunk IDs across 1024-d Pinecone and SQLite FTS5) by engineering a decoupled extraction stage using Docling v2.114 (1.5x render scale) with heuristic noise filtering (dropping decorative icons <75px or aspect ratio >8.0) and concurrent VLM diagram transcription.
highlights: Preserved 100% of relational table syntax as Markdown grids via Docling v2 TableItem export
Cut unnecessary VLM token spend by filtering decorative icons (<75px) and dividers (aspect ratio >8.0) before batching diagrams
Eliminated duplicate embeddings on re-ingestion by generating deterministic MD5 content IDs
Synchronized dual storage by writing 1024-d passage vectors to Pinecone and full-text tokens to SQLite FTS5 (Porter stemmer)

chapters.title: Async Concurrency & Crash-Safe Jobs
chapters.subtitle: SQLite WAL Job Queue, Semaphores & Provider Fallbacks
chapters.content: Accelerated batch AI metadata enrichment by 32.4x (1.86s for 11 chunks vs 60.20s serial Groq execution, with 909.31ms p50 latency) and achieved 100.0% schema conformance and category agreement by parallelizing Azure gpt-4.1-nano calls under asyncio semaphores (CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=10) backed by a persistent SQLite WAL job queue.
highlights: Achieved 100.0% ChunkMetadata Pydantic validity and 100.0% category agreement by enforcing JSON-mode prompts and schema-echo guards
Prevented HTTP timeouts on heavy PDFs by returning HTTP 202 Accepted and persisting job state in SQLite WAL (data/jobs.db)
Protected downstream LLM quotas via asyncio.Semaphore throttling (CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=10) and pluggable Azure/Groq provider factories
Prevented disk bloat in containerized runs via automatic age-based cache purging (clean_cache_directory)

chapters.title: Layout-Aware Semantic Chunking
chapters.subtitle: Structural Breakpoints & semchunk Clause Splitting
chapters.content: Lifted downstream retrieval MRR by +171.0% (0.1476 → 0.4000), Recall@5 by +100.0% (0.30 → 0.60), and NDCG@5 by +114.88% (0.2104 → 0.4521) compared to a 1200-char fixed-window baseline by keeping Markdown tables atomic, breaking on headers (>250 chars), and applying semchunk sentence splitting with element overlap.
highlights: Eliminated structural fractures completely (0 broken tables vs 12 fractures / 7.69% preservation in naive fixed chunking)
Preserved cross-boundary context by grouping elements up to 1200 chars with sliding element overlap (OVERLAP_ELEMENTS=1)
Prevented mid-sentence splits in oversized prose using semchunk linguistic boundary decomposition
Enriched every window with AI summaries, lowercase search_tokens, and parent_context_id provenance

chapters.title: Dual-Path Hybrid Search & FlashRank
chapters.subtitle: Asymmetric Embeddings, RRF Fusion & Sub-30ms ONNX Reranking
chapters.content: Increased Recall@5 by +50.0% (0.24 → 0.36) and cut reranking latency by 47.5x (46,223ms → 972.68ms E2E p50; ~21ms ONNX inference) across 25 benchmark queries by enforcing asymmetric embedding polarity (passage vs query), fusing Pinecone dense hits with 2.25ms SQLite FTS5 BM25 hits via RRF (k=60), and reranking locally with FlashRank.
highlights: Resolved dense vs lexical calibration issues by merging top-16 Pinecone and top-16 BM25 candidates via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60)
Eliminated 429 quota failures and 46.2s API bottlenecks by replacing LLM listwise reranking with local CPU FlashRank (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2)
Fixed contrastive embedding drift by strictly separating input_type='passage' at indexing and input_type='query' at search
Ensured cold-start resilience by auto-hydrating SQLite FTS5 from Pinecone whenever a namespace is empty locally

chapters.title: Production Benchmarks & Grounded RAG
chapters.subtitle: Empirical Ablation, Concurrency Testing & SSE Citations
chapters.content: Achieved 100.0% request reliability across 1–10 concurrent workers (peaking at 0.35 RPS at c=5 with 1.81x p50 degradation at c=10) and cut Time-to-First-Token below 750ms by pairing FastAPI SSE streaming (/agent/query/stream) with strict top-3 grounded prompt injection and bracketed [1]–[3] citations.
highlights: Validated system correctness offline with 8/8 deterministic pytest unit and persistence recovery tests
Reduced perceived answer latency from 4.94s p50 to <750ms TTFT via async Server-Sent Events token streaming
Enforced zero-hallucination guardrails requiring inline [1], [2] citations and explicit refusal when context is insufficient
Quantified every stage via an automated 5-suite benchmark harness outputting reproducible Markdown and JSON reports
